name: Elah
overview: Elah was a male figure noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Hoshea, who became King of Israel. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His significance is tied directly to his role as progenitor of a key Israelite monarch.
namesAndTitles: The name Elah means "species of a mighty tree," reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This single name does not appear to be given by God but carries a natural imagery that may imply strength or stability.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Elah as the father of Hoshea, the King of Israel, establishing a direct familial link to the Israelite monarchy. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Elah's importance in the biblical narrative stems from his connection to Hoshea, the last king of Israel before the kingdom's fall. Through Elah, the lineage and legitimacy of Hoshea's kingship are established, marking him as a figure of historical and theological interest within the history of Israel's monarchy.
